title: The henselization of a pair is flat with the same quotients by powers of the ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal and $(A^h,I^h)$, $I^h=IA^h$, the henselization of the pair $(A,I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], with structure map $\eta:A\to A^h$. Then $\eta$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and for every $n\ge1$ the ring map $A/I^n\to A^h/I^nA^h$ induced by $\eta$ is an isomorphism (note $I^nA^h=(I^h)^n$).

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGU (lemma-henselization-flat, line 3105) and its proof (étale maps are flat, Algebra Lemma Tag 00U2; filtered colimits of flat modules are flat, Algebra Lemma Tag 05UT lemma-colimit-flat; $A/I^n\to B/I^nB$ isomorphisms by flatness, Algebra Lemma Tag 051H; colimit over the category of [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization])

proof.text: *Filtered-colimit set-up.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization] to $(A,I)$. Its directed category $\mathcal C$ has objects the etale $A$-algebras $A\to B$ for which $A/I\to B/IB$ is an isomorphism, and it constructs $A^h=\varinjlim_{B\in\mathcal C}B$ with $I^h=IA^h$. Since $I^h$ is generated by the image of $I$, $(I^h)^n=I^nA^h$ for every $n\ge1$ (products of generators give both inclusions).

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGU, proof (line 3105): the construction in Lemma 0A02 expresses $A^h$ as a filtered colimit of etale $A$-algebras with $A/I\cong B/IB$ and $I^h=IA^h$

proof.text: *$u:A\to A^h$ is flat.* For every object $A\to B$ of $\mathcal C$, the map $A\to B$ is flat because it is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. Regard the $B$ as $A$-modules; their filtered colimit is the underlying $A$-module of $A^h$ by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-flat-modules] says this $A$-module is flat, which is exactly that $u$ is a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGU, proof: etale maps are flat (Algebra Lemma 00U2) and a filtered colimit of flat modules is flat (Algebra Lemma 05UT)

proof.text: *The quotient maps for each stage.* Fix $n\ge1$ and an object $A\to B$ of $\mathcal C$. The map $A\to B$ is flat by step 2 and $A/I\to B/IB$ is an isomorphism by the definition of $\mathcal C$, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-iso-mod-ideal-powers] gives an isomorphism $\beta_{B,n}:A/I^n\xrightarrow{\sim}B/I^nB$. These isomorphisms are compatible with every morphism in $\mathcal C$, because all maps are induced by the same $A$-algebra maps and reduction modulo $I^n$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGU, proof (line 3105): for each etale $A$-algebra $B$ in the henselization system, flatness and $A/I\cong B/IB$ imply $A/I^n\cong B/I^nB$ by Algebra Lemma 051H

proof.text: *Pass to the colimit.* The compatible family $\beta_{B,n}$ identifies the constant diagram $B\mapsto A/I^n$ with the diagram $B\mapsto B/I^nB$. The index category $\mathcal C$ is nonempty filtered, hence connected; by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram] its colimit of the constant diagram is $A/I^n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise], quotienting the filtered colimit $A^h=\varinjlim B$ by the ideal generated by the image of $I^n$ is the colimit of the quotients $B/I^nB$. Thus the induced map $A/I^n\to A^h/I^nA^h$ is an isomorphism. Together with steps 1 and 2, this proves the statement for every $n\ge1$.
